meta.name: sanvi-frontend performance profiles
meta.emulationNote: Every profile here is Chrome/WebKit EMULATION (CPU slowdown + network shaping), not a physical mid-range Android or iOS device. Real-device testing is parked in docs/release/needs-humans.md. Every number this phase produces is a lab number and says so: excellent for catching a regression between two builds, silent about what a real user on a real phone experiences.
meta.inpNote: INP is a field metric and cannot be measured in a lab. Total Blocking Time is the proxy the gates assert, and anything labelled INP in these harnesses is a mislabel by definition (NFR-1101).
meta.comparabilityNote: Measurements are comparable only under the same pins and the same profile. Artifacts record the profile block they ran under; bench-compare refuses to compare artifacts whose profiles differ. A runner upgrade is a deliberate commit that changes this file, never a silent drift.
meta.localeCoverageNote: Lighthouse drives the SSR apps (storefront, marketing) per locale through their /{locale} URL prefixes. The SPAs (admin, platform-admin) negotiate locale from the sanvi_locale cookie, which Lighthouse cannot set, so SPA Lighthouse runs report the default locale only — recorded honestly per artifact, not hidden. The axe sweep covers both locales for all four apps via cookie or prefix.

midrange-android.description: Lighthouse's default emulated mid-range Android mobile: 4x CPU slowdown on a slow 4G shape. The profile the Lighthouse harness runs under.

ios-safari.description: Emulated iPhone via Playwright's device descriptor. Lighthouse cannot emulate WebKit (Chromium-only), so this profile drives the Playwright-based sweeps only — never Lighthouse. Device testing itself is parked in docs/release/needs-humans.md.

budget.profileNote: Static gzip file sizes off the build output — no runtime profile applies. Same build, same numbers.

lighthouse.runsNote: 3 runs per URL; the median is what artifacts record. Three runs is the minimum that survives one noisy run.

axe.localesNote: SvelteKit apps via the /{locale} URL prefix; SPAs via the sanvi_locale cookie set before navigation.

harness.runsNote: 3 runs per URL; the median is what artifacts record. Three runs is the minimum that survives one noisy run.
